Subject: Redwood response - DPA redlines (line items)
Attachments: redline_comments_hp_v2.docx (DOCX, 28KB)

Julia — appreciate the thorough review. Below are counsel's high-level responses; see attached for inline redline suggestions and justification.

1) Transfers: Redwood's default is the EU SCCs (controller-processor addendum); we can append an executed EU-US addendum if HealthPrime requires a second signature flow. Legal note: SCCs plus our technical safeguards (encryption at-rest/in-transit, KMS integrations) are how we operationalize lawful transfers.

2) Subprocessors: We agree to provide a signed appendix listing subprocessors at time of execution and commit to 30 days' notice for additions. For "onboarding evidence", we can supply a table of third-party audit statuses (SOC 2 summary, ISO statements, pen-test date) but cannot disclose full reports without an NDA/TA.

3) Retention: We are open to a 90-day backup retention cap for regulated data classes; propose to carve out system telemetry and logs for operational troubleshooting with a 180-day window — happy to map by data category.

4) Liability/flowdowns: We can accept certain flow-downs to subprocessors but will need to preserve a common-sense cap tied to fees. See redline for suggested language.

Execution path: Redwood typically facilitates execution via AdobeSign (preferred) but can use DocuSign if required by procurement. If HealthPrime prefers AdobeSign, we can prepare the envelope and include the subprocessor appendix as an attached exhibit.

Next steps proposed:
- HealthPrime confirms whether SCCs or EU-US addendum preferred (reply by EOD Mon).
- Agree on the backup retention windows and data category mapping.
- Confirm NDA requirement for sharing full SOC/pen-test artifacts (legal/email ok).

I'll follow up with a consolidated redline (v2) if you confirm transfer mechanism.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
